title: Characterization of nonreducible associative idempotent monotone functions
statement:
Let $X$ be a totally ordered Abelian group with respect to addition, and let $F:X^n\to X$ be an associative, idempotent, monotone function. The function $F$ is **reducible** if there exists an associative binary function $G:X^2\to X$ such that $F$ is obtained by iterating $G$; otherwise it is nonreducible. **Nonreducibility conjecture.** The function $F$ is not reducible if and only if $n$ is odd and there exists a monotone bijection $g:X\to X$ such that

$$
F(x_1,x_2,\dots,x_n)=g^{-1}\left(\sum_{i=1}^n(-1)^i g(x_i)\right).
$$

This would characterize the associative idempotent monotone functions that are not reducible, extending the known reducibility results beyond the nondecreasing case. The source presents the characterization as an open conjecture.
source_name: Gergely Kiss and Gábor Somlai, “Associative idempotent nondecreasing functions are reducible”, arXiv:1707.04341 (2018).
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.04341

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2017).
